demo.title: A request is not permission.
demo.intro: Interactive illustration only. This runs in your browser and is not connected to any infrastructure. Try the request, then approve that exact revision as the simulated human reviewer.
demo.approvalLabel: Approval applies only to the target, operation and revision shown above.
demo.initial: DENIED · production/payment-api is outside staging/*. No human approval is recorded.
demo.denied: DENIED · The action is outside the standing scope or no longer matches the current approval. Stop for human review.
demo.approved: APPROVAL RECORDED · Simulated approval is bound to the displayed target, operation and revision. Evaluate the request again.
demo.allowed: EXECUTION ALLOWED · This exact request has standing staging authority or matching simulated human approval. No real action has run.
demo.invalidated: APPROVAL REVOKED · The request changed. Any previous approval is invalid, even if you change the values back.
demo.evidence: Illustrative evidence: identity workflow-agent-17; target and revision; policy decision; approval binding. After a real action, verify observed state against approved intent and reconcile any mismatch.
demo.static: A restart of production/payment-api by workflow-agent-17, authorized for staging/*, is denied. Explicit human approval for that target, restart operation and revision 182 permits only that exact request. Identity and permissions come from the trusted execution layer, never from what an LLM claims.

sections.title: The hard part is not calling an LLM.
sections.body: Your applications, APIs, data, identities, approvals and operating procedures already exist. The engineering work is connecting them safely and usefully. We take on that integration burden, working with the environment you trust.

sections.title: Fit the business. Make authority explicit.
sections.body: Governed AI that works with your business, not around it.

items.title: Use your existing systems
items.body: No re-engineering around us. Integrate with the systems, data, identities and workflows your organization already uses.

items.title: No implicit authority
items.body: Each agent has explicit identity, permissions, scope and approval. Claiming authority in a prompt cannot create it.

items.title: Humans stay in control
items.body: Automate authorized routine work. Escalate risk, uncertainty and exceptional conditions to the people responsible.

sections.title: From infrastructure decisions to working systems.
sections.body: Architecture guidance, hands-on engineering and technical enablement for enterprise teams and SI partners.

items.title: Infrastructure & migration
items.body: Platform architecture, dependency discovery, container and virtualization choices, staged migration plans and operational handover.

items.title: Private AI & governed workflows
items.body: Model placement, enterprise integration and controlled agent execution on infrastructure that fits your security and operating requirements.

items.title: SI partner enablement
items.body: Solution design reviews, technical workshops, proof-of-concept planning and delivery guidance for Thailand's SI engineering teams.

sections.title: AI handles volume. Humans handle judgment.
sections.body: Do not make people rubber-stamp every routine result. Route the right cases to review, using explicit rules and evidence.

items.title: Normal result
items.body: Continue within the approved workflow.

items.title: High value, missing evidence or conflicting data
items.body: Pause for human review.

items.title: Low confidence
items.body: Escalate uncertainty; do not invent certainty.

items.title: Policy violation
items.body: Block the action and request human review.

items.title: Large blast radius
items.body: Require explicit approval before execution.

sections.title: Infrastructure expertise, applied directly.
sections.body: Work with a principal engineer on the decisions that shape reliability, operability and the path to production.

items.title: Architecture & migration
items.body: Assess the platform, map dependencies and compare container, virtualization and private-cloud options. Deliver architecture decisions, a phased migration plan, validation criteria and rollback considerations.

items.title: Private AI infrastructure
items.body: Plan compute, model serving, data access, identity and operational ownership. Evaluate local, enterprise-hosted and approved API options against workload requirements, not a universal model preference.

items.title: SI technical enablement
items.body: Support solution qualification, architecture reviews, workshops and proof-of-concept design. Help partner engineers understand the trade-offs, validate the solution and take ownership of delivery.

sections.title: Four ways to connect AI to the business.
sections.body: Light supplies a reusable governance and execution foundation. The engagement adapts it to your data, identities, systems and approval processes.

items.title: Enterprise AI Workflow Engineering
items.body: Turn an existing process into an AI-assisted workflow: connect authoritative data, define the reasoning task, structure outputs and establish human checkpoints. Applicable to finance, procurement, compliance, operations, support, sales operations, manufacturing, logistics, documents, reporting and IT.

items.title: Governed Agent Operations
items.body: Define durable workload identity, authorization, scoped tool access and mutation boundaries. Integrate human approvals, policy checks, execution audit and post-action reconciliation. The model proposes; the platform decides whether execution is allowed.

items.title: Service & Dependency Intelligence
items.body: Build an evidence-backed service graph from repositories, configuration, runtime, infrastructure and documentation. Discover dependencies and owners, detect changes, assess blast radius, prepare impact reports, notify affected teams and support migrations and incident investigation.

items.title: Custom Enterprise AI Solution
items.body: Design a bounded solution around the customer's own data and operating model when a packaged product does not fit. Prepare context, reason, produce structured output, validate it and return the result to the existing workflow through a human or policy boundary.

sections.title: AI Workflow Continuous Optimization.
sections.body: Review human corrections, rejected outputs, escalations, exceptions, false positives and negatives, latency, model performance, data changes and business rules. AI can prepare improvements; changes are tested, reviewed and released as controlled workflow revisions. Production policy never changes silently.

platform.title: Light: a governed execution foundation for enterprise AI
platform.description: Separate flexible AI reasoning from controlled execution. Integrate Light with enterprise systems, private models, frontier APIs and optional Nutanix AI infrastructure.
platform.headline: Loose on reasoning. Rigid on control.
platform.lede: Light is the reusable execution and governance foundation beneath the solution. It governs the actions surrounding a probabilistic model; it does not make the LLM deterministic.

sections.title: Keep model choice separate from authority.
sections.body: Local, enterprise-hosted and frontier models can support agents. Light governs identity, authorization, scope, approval, tool access, state, audit, execution and reconciliation before those agents interact with your systems.

sections.title: Flexible data. Unambiguous control.
sections.body: Customer-specific information should not require rebuilding the whole platform. Combine known control fields, flexible business payloads, evidence, reasoning instructions and structured output.

items.title: Controlled structured fields
items.body: Authorization, routing, enforcement, thresholds and state transitions use explicit structured data. A sentence in a business document does not grant permission.

items.title: Flexible business payload
items.body: Documents, text and JSON carry domain-specific context. Keep their evidence and reasoning instructions separate from trusted control fields.

items.title: Validated output
items.body: Check structured output against the workflow contract, then apply the human or policy boundary before returning it to an existing process.

sections.title: Use the model that fits the workload.
sections.body: Choose according to security, capability, performance and cost. Governance stays consistent across providers; no model is universally superior.

items.title: Local / private models
items.body: A placement option for sensitive data, subject to the organization's data controls and operating capacity.

items.title: Enterprise-hosted AI
items.body: Controlled serving and access for workloads within your enterprise platform.

items.title: Frontier APIs
items.body: An option for difficult reasoning when data policy permits the external service.

items.title: Smaller models
items.body: Evaluate focused models for classification, extraction and routine processing.

governance.title: AI governance: explicit identity, scope & human approval
governance.description: See how a scoped agent request is denied, how exact human approval changes authorization and why AI identity cannot be claimed in a prompt.
governance.headline: The model proposes. Authority lives elsewhere.
governance.lede: AI reasoning can be flexible. Enterprise execution must remain controlled. Identity, permissions and approval come from the trusted execution layer — not from what an LLM says.

sections.title: Staging authority does not include production.
sections.body: The same proposed action can be useful and unauthorized. A policy decision must happen before execution, not after it.

sections.title: Check the request. Preserve the evidence.
sections.body: Define the controls for each workflow as part of the integration, including how to stop and who can approve an exception.

items.title: Identity & authorization
items.body: Use trusted workload identity and explicit permissions. A model cannot inherit another agent's authority by claiming its name.

items.title: Scope & approval
items.body: Bind tool access and changes to approved targets, operations and revision. Changed intent requires fresh approval.

items.title: State & audit
items.body: Record the request, policy decision, approval and execution outcome so a reviewer can reconstruct what was authorized and what happened.

items.title: Verify & reconcile
items.body: Compare observed state with approved intent. Surface partial failures, unexpected changes and unresolved outcomes for accountable follow-up.

sections.title: Human attention goes where it matters.
sections.body: AI handles volume. Humans handle judgment. Review conditions are explicit, not a request to blindly trust a confidence score.

items.title: Normal result
items.body: Process within the pre-approved policy.

items.title: High-value transaction
items.body: Require human review.

items.title: Missing evidence / conflicting data
items.body: Pause and ask a responsible reviewer.

items.title: Low confidence
items.body: Escalate rather than assume.

items.title: Policy violation
items.body: Block execution and route to review.

items.title: Large blast radius
items.body: Require explicit approval.

how-we-work.title: How we work: understand, integrate, govern & improve
how-we-work.description: An infrastructure-led engagement with clear outcomes, authoritative evidence, integration, human approval boundaries and controlled production improvements.
how-we-work.headline: A working system starts with shared understanding.
how-we-work.lede: We carry the integration burden. Your team retains ownership of business decisions, operating responsibilities and authority boundaries.

sections.title: Make the outcome and boundaries explicit.
sections.body: Scope the work around your environment. Agree deliverables and verification criteria before building.

items.title: Understand
items.body: Identify the desired outcome, required evidence, authoritative data, decision and action boundaries, and human responsibilities. Map the current infrastructure and workflow.

items.title: Integrate
items.body: Connect systems, APIs, databases, documents, infrastructure, identity and existing workflows. Prepare context from evidence and return validated outputs to the process people use.

items.title: Govern
items.body: Define agent identity, permissions, scope, approval gates, escalation, validation and audit requirements. Test the refused paths as well as the permitted ones.

items.title: Operate & Improve
items.body: Verify production outcomes, hand over operational knowledge and review corrections and exceptions. Test, review and release changes as explicit workflow revisions.

sections.title: Reasoning is one part of the workflow.
sections.body: The same pattern supports IT operations and business processes. Data enters as evidence; it does not become authority.

items.title: Enterprise data
items.body: Use authoritative sources.

items.title: Context preparation
items.body: Select relevant evidence.

items.title: AI reasoning
items.body: Apply explicit instructions.

items.title: Structured output
items.body: Produce a defined result.

items.title: Validation
items.body: Check the result and evidence.

items.title: Human / policy boundary
items.body: Check permission before action.

items.title: Existing workflow
items.body: Integrate, verify and reconcile.

sections.title: Your systems. Your judgment. Clear ownership.
sections.body: Integrate AI into a real business workflow. Give each agent only the authority its role requires. Use systems and processes your organization already trusts. Verify, govern and audit what AI is allowed to do. Automation should make your people more capable, not remove them from accountable decisions.
